summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma was admitted for scheduled maintenance chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate. He tolerated the infusion well, with methotrexate levels declining appropriately to 0.13 by discharge, indicating effective clearance. He remained stable throughout the admission, with no significant complications. Mild transaminitis was noted, likely due to methotrexate, and was expected to resolve. His chronic conditions, including diabetes insipidus and hypertension, were managed without issue. He reported intermittent upper abdominal and chest discomfort, deemed non-cardiac and likely due to gas or muscle spasm, with follow-up recommended post-discharge. He was discharged home with instructions to complete a short course of leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, continue his regular medications, and resume rituximab and temozolomide when insurance coverage allows. The next chemotherapy cycle is scheduled in four months.
